paper.title: Reducing Dueling Bandits to Cardinal Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Utility-Based Dueling Bandits (UBDB) over an arbitrary arm set X, linear link
unmapped: Arbitrary (possibly infinite) arm set X with structure exploited by a black-box MAB algorithm (SBM)
Regret measured on unobserved average utility (u_t+v_t)/2
settings.definition_quote: In the utility based dueling bandit game (UBDB), the algorithm chooses $(x_t, y_t)\in X\times X$ at each step, and a corresponding pair of random utilities $(u_t, v_t) \in[0,1]$ are given rise to, but not observed by the algorithm. ... The linear link function $\philin$ is defined by $\Pr[b_t = 1 | (u_t,v_t)] = \philin(u_t, v_t) \eqdef \frac{ 1+v_t - u_t} 2$

settings.name_in_paper: UBDB over a finite set X of cardinality K, linear link
unmapped: Regret measured on unobserved average utility (u_t+v_t)/2

settings.name_in_paper: UBDB over a compact convex set X in R^d with linear expected utility, linear link
unmapped: Regret measured on unobserved average utility (u_t+v_t)/2
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, the set $X$ of arms is an arbitrary (infinite) convex set in $\R^d$. Here, the player chooses at each time point a vector $x \in X$ and observes a stochastic reward with an expected value of $\dotprod{\mu}{x}$

settings.name_in_paper: UBDB, polytope X in the Delta-gap case, linear link
unmapped: Regret measured on unobserved average utility (u_t+v_t)/2
settings.definition_quote: In case $X$ is a polytope with vertex set $V$ and there is a unique vertex $v^*\in V$ achieving $\max_{x\in X} \dotprod{\mu}{x}$, and any other vertex $v\in V$ satisfies the gap condition $\dotprod{\mu}{v} \leq \dotprod{\mu}{v^*} - \Delta$ for some $\Delta>0$, we say we are in the $\Delta$-gap case.

settings.name_in_paper: Dueling bandits with preferences satisfying the Relaxed Extended Stochastic Triangle Inequality (finite X)
unmapped: Preference probabilities 0.5+Delta(x,y) satisfying the Relaxed Extended Stochastic Triangle Inequality with parameter gamma: gamma*Delta(x*,y) <= Delta(x*,x)+Delta(x,y)
settings.definition_quote: (Relaxed) Extended Stochastic Triangle Inequality. For some $\gamma \geq 1$, and any pair $x,y$ (where it does not necessarily hold that $x \succ y$) it holds that $\gamma\Delta(x^*,y) \leq \Delta(x^*,x)+\Delta(x,y)$.

symbols.c_sbm: constant in the black-box SBM expected regret bound c log^alpha T
symbols.alpha_sbm: exponent of log T in the SBM regret bound

conditions: The black-box SBM has expected regret at most c log^alpha T after T steps, for all T (and over all utility distributions)

source.label: thm:infinite
source.quote: Assume the SBM $S$ in Line~\ref{line:SBM} of $\Doubler$ (Algorithm~\ref{alg:infinite}) has an expected regret of $c \log^\alpha T$ after $T$ steps, for all $T$.  Then the expected regret of $\Doubler$ is at most $2c\frac{\alpha}{\alpha+1}\log^{\alpha+1} T$.

results.notes: Black-box reduction; regret defined via expectation of mu(x*) - average utility, i.e. pseudo-regret.

symbols.f_SBM: expected regret bound f(T) = Omega(T^alpha), alpha>0, of the black-box SBM

conditions: The SBM's expected regret is bounded by f(T) = Omega(T^alpha) with alpha > 0

source.label: thm:infinite
source.quote: If the expected regret of the SBM is bounded by some function $f(T)=\Omega(T^\alpha)$ (with $\alpha>0$),  then the expected regret of $\Doubler$ is at most $O(f(T))$.

conditions: X is a compact convex set
tuning: SBM = ConfidenceBall_2 of Dani et al. (as stated in the corollary)

source.label: cor:finite
source.quote: Assume that the SBM $S$ in Line~\ref{line:SBM} of $\Doubler$ is algorithm \confballtwo (resp.\ \confballone). If $X$ is a compact convex set, then the expected regret of $\Doubler$ is at most $O(\sqrt{dT\log^3(T)})$ (resp.\ $O(\sqrt{d^2T\log^3(T)})$).

results.notes: Corollary attributes sqrt(dT log^3 T) to ConfidenceBall_2, while Lemma 2.3 attributes it to ConfidenceBall_1; recorded as stated. Horizon knowledge for Dani et al.'s algorithm not stated explicitly.

conditions: X is a compact convex set
tuning: SBM = ConfidenceBall_1 of Dani et al. (as stated in the corollary)

source.label: cor:finite
source.quote: If $X$ is a compact convex set, then the expected regret of $\Doubler$ is at most $O(\sqrt{dT\log^3(T)})$ (resp.\ $O(\sqrt{d^2T\log^3(T)})$).

results.notes: The resp. assignment of ConfidenceBall_1/2 is swapped relative to Lemma 2.3; recorded as stated.

conditions: Delta-gap case: X a polytope with unique optimal vertex and vertex gap Delta
tuning: SBM = ConfidenceBall_2 (as stated in the corollary)

source.label: cor:finite
source.quote: In the $\Delta$-gap setting (see discussion leading to Lemma~\ref{lem:confball gap}), the expected regret is bounded by $O\left( \Delta^{-1}d^2 \log^4(T) \right)$ (resp.\ $O\left( \Delta^{-1}d^3 \log^4(T) \right)$).

results.notes: Delta is the vertex gap (Dani et al. sense), mapped to Delta_lin. ConfidenceBall_1/2 assignment swapped vs Lemma 2.4; recorded as stated.

conditions: Delta-gap case: X a polytope with unique optimal vertex and vertex gap Delta
tuning: SBM = ConfidenceBall_1 (as stated in the corollary)

source.label: cor:finite
source.quote: In the $\Delta$-gap setting ..., the expected regret is bounded by $O\left( \Delta^{-1}d^2 \log^4(T) \right)$ (resp.\ $O\left( \Delta^{-1}d^3 \log^4(T) \right)$).

source.label: cor:infinite
source.quote: Consider a  UBDB game over a finite set $X$ of cardinality $K$. Let $\Delta_i$ be the difference between the reward of the best arm and the $i$'th best arm. Assume  the SBM $S$ in Line~\ref{line:SBM} of $\Doubler$ is  UCB. Then the expected regret of $\Doubler$  is at most $O(H \log^2(T))$ where $H \eqdef \sum_{i=2}^K \Delta_i^{-1}$

results.notes: H = sum of inverse gaps. Setting s1 lists T in learner_knows for MultiSBM; Doubler with UCB does not need T.

bound.expression_latex: O\!\left(\! H \alpha\ln T + H\alpha\left(\!K\ln K\!+\!K\ln\ln T -\!\!\sum\nolimits_{x \neq x^*} \!\ln \Delta_x\!\right) \!\!\right)

symbols.alpha_r: robustness parameter of the SBM policy, alpha = max(3, ln K / ln ln T)

tuning: SBMs are alpha-robust with alpha = max(3, ln(K)/ln ln(T)), e.g. UCB (Algorithm 1) with parameter alpha

source.label: thm:alg2bound
source.quote: The total expected regret of $\MultiSbm$ (Algorithm~\ref{alg:K TBMs}) in the UBDB game is $O( H \alpha\ln T + H\alpha(K\ln K+K\ln\ln T -\sum_{x \neq x^*} \ln \Delta_x))$, assuming the policy of the SBMs defined in Line~\ref{line:SBMsInit} is $\alpha$-robust for $\alpha=\max(3, \ln(K)/\ln\ln(T))$. The robustness can be ensured by choosing the UCB policy (Algorithm~\ref{alg:ucb}) for the SBM with parameter $\alpha$.

results.notes: H = sum over suboptimal arms of 1/Delta_x. alpha depends on T, so horizon known.

symbols.gamma_tri: parameter gamma >= 1 of the Relaxed Extended Stochastic Triangle Inequality
symbols.alpha_r: robustness parameter alpha = max(3, ln K / ln ln T)

conditions: Duel outcome probabilities satisfy Relaxed Extended Stochastic Triangle Inequality with parameter gamma
tuning: MAB policy alpha-robust with alpha = max(3, ln(K)/ln ln(T))

source.label: thm:alg2bound_extended
source.quote: Assume the probability for the outcome of a duel is defined according to $\Delta(x,y)$, where $\Delta$ has the Relaxed Extended Stochastic Triangle Inequality with parameter $\gamma$. The total expected regret of $\MultiSbm$ in the UBDB game is asymptotic to $$\gamma H\alpha \left(K\ln(K)+K\ln\ln(T) +\sum_{x \in X\setminus\{x^*\}} \ln(1/\Delta_x)\right)  + \ln(T)  H \alpha $$ assuming the invoked MAB policy is $\alpha$-robust for $\alpha=\max(3, \ln(K)/\ln\ln(T))$.

results.notes: 'Asymptotic to' interpreted as an O bound; proof deferred to full version. Meaning of Delta_x in this general model not fully specified.
